name: Garlic & Thyme Roast Chicken, Buttery Mash, Tenderstem & Light Cream Gravy
description: Pan-seared boneless chicken thighs finished in the oven, with buttery mash, tenderstem broccoli and a light shallot, chicken stock and cream gravy made in the roasting pan. Uses one ovenproof frying pan and one saucepan. Approximate macros use skinless thighs; skin-on thighs also work.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Use a frying pan whose handle and coating are oven-safe at this temperature. Cut the potatoes into even 2-3 cm chunks, place in a saucepan, cover with cold salted water and bring to the boil. Simmer for 15-18 minutes until tender, leaving room to add the broccoli later.

Pat the boneless chicken thighs dry, open them out and season with salt and black pepper. Heat 1 tsp olive oil in the ovenproof frying pan over medium-high heat. Sear the smooth side, or skin side if using skin-on thighs, for 4-5 minutes until golden, then turn and sear for 1-2 minutes. For skin-on thighs, use medium heat and allow 5-7 minutes on the skin side to render the fat.

Lightly crush the peeled garlic clove and add it to the pan with 1/2 tsp dried thyme. Turn the thighs golden side up and transfer the pan to the oven. Roast for about 10-15 minutes, depending on thickness, until the thickest part reaches 75°C. Begin checking smaller thighs earlier.

While the chicken roasts, finely chop the shallot. Dissolve 1/4 chicken stock cube in 100 ml hot water, adjusting the amount of cube to the packet dilution if needed. Add the tenderstem broccoli to the potato saucepan for the final 3-4 minutes, until just tender. Lift it out with tongs onto the serving plate and keep warm.
Drain the potatoes using the saucepan lid, let them steam-dry for 1-2 minutes, then mash in the same saucepan with 15 g butter and 50 ml milk. Season to taste and cover to keep warm.

Using an oven glove, remove the chicken pan from the oven and transfer the thighs to the serving plate to rest for 5 minutes. Keep the hot pan handle covered with a dry oven glove while making the gravy. Leave about 1 tsp fat and the browned juices in the pan, spooning away excess fat if necessary.

Set the frying pan over medium-low heat and soften the chopped shallot for 2-3 minutes, adding a splash of water if the pan is dry. Mash the roasted garlic into the pan juices. Pour in the prepared chicken stock, scrape up the browned bits and simmer for 2-3 minutes until slightly reduced.

Stir in 25 ml double cream, 1/2 tsp Dijon mustard and any chicken resting juices. Simmer gently for 1-2 minutes, keeping the gravy light and pourable; loosen with a splash of water if needed. Taste before adding salt and pepper. Serve the chicken with the mash, broccoli and gravy, spooning the gravy around the chicken if keeping crisp skin.
